title: Valid Anagram
description: Count character differences in a 26-slot list. Equal lengths and zero final counts mean the strings are anagrams.
note: The input is assumed to contain only lowercase English letters a–z. Subtracting 'a' from a character maps it to an index from 0 through 25.
notes: list(26, 0) creates 26 initialized integer slots. This keeps the fixed-alphabet representation from the Python solution and avoids hash-table operations.

Subtracting two characters returns the difference of their Unicode scalar values as an int. c1 - 'a' gives the slot for a lowercase English letter. The .code property remains available for raw scalar values; this indexing scheme is not a general Unicode anagram algorithm.

Each zipped pair increments the count for the first string and decrements the count for the second. Birdie’s zip requires equal lengths; the early size check returns false before a mismatch could raise an error.
all(v == 0 for v in freqs) checks counts lazily and stops at the first nonzero value. It does not allocate an intermediate list of booleans.
In the usual unit-cost model, the algorithm takes O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space using 26 counter slots. Birdie’s arbitrary-precision integer operations still depend on operand size.

The draft counter API also permits counter(s) == counter(t), comparing character frequencies independently of insertion order. This example keeps the explicit array-based algorithm as its primary solution.
